# mvpfy

> mvpfy ("mvpfy by feature1") is a free, MIT-licensed, open-source desktop IDE for product
> builders. It runs an existing codebase locally in Docker with a live preview and an
> embedded VS Code (code-server) editor, lets someone non-technical describe changes in
> plain language that an AI coding agent (Claude Code, optionally Codex CLI) applies, and
> checks the product for what stands between it and real users. Two audiences: a product
> manager at a company, whose changes exit as pull requests engineers review; and a solo
> builder taking an AI-built prototype (Lovable, Replit, Bolt, v0, Emergent) to production.

Key facts:
- Positioning: "The IDE for product builders." Like Lovable or Replit, but for a codebase
  that already exists, running locally, with a pull request (not a deploy) as the output.
- Prototype-to-production: mvpfy audits an app for launch blockers and reports them in
  plain language, graded — a "blocker" means real people lose money, lose data, or get
  access they should not have. Typical findings on an AI-built prototype: the demo login
  still works so anyone can sign in as a full user; the database lives inside the
  container and is wiped on every deploy; checkout runs against test keys or a mock so
  customers are never charged; the session secret is a placeholder shared by every copy of
  the code; features were switched off to make local running possible and now return
  nothing; there is no error tracking so failures are silent. Fixing these is a list of
  specific changes, not a rewrite.
- Why the audit is reliable: mvpfy sets the local environment up itself, so it knows which
  parts of the product are stand-ins it created rather than inferring intent from code.
  Findings cite the file that proves them; the verdict is computed by mvpfy from the
  findings, never asserted by the agent; and a builder can accept a blocker to launch
  anyway, which keeps it on the list marked as their decision rather than clearing it.
- vs Cursor/Windsurf: those are code-first tools for engineers (unit of work: a diff).
  mvpfy is product-first (unit of work: a plain-language change or a user story); the PM
  never reads a diff.
- Runs on macOS (primary), Linux, Windows (experimental beta). Electron + React.
- Requires locally installed: git, GitHub CLI (gh), Docker Desktop, Claude Code (signed
  in). Codex CLI optional. Agent runs bill to the user's own Anthropic/OpenAI account.
- Privacy: no mvpfy server; repos and the running product stay on the user's machine.
  Code is sent to the model API only via the user's own agent CLI.
- Features: one-click Docker bootstrap with open-source stand-ins (Postgres, Redis,
  MailHog) for missing services; live app preview and embedded VS Code in tabs; demo
  logins and an editable env-vars card; plain-language change requests ("Ask mvpfy");
  self-healing failed runs (plain-English diagnosis + one-click fix/retry); container log
  streaming; repo sync; feature planning in the Feature1 style — a minimal PRD the PM
  reviews and agrees, then user stories with acceptance criteria on a per-feature board
  (To do → Coding → Testing → Done), each story implemented by the agent and shipped as a
  pull request the PM tests before marking done; multiple features plannable in parallel,
  each with its own board; launch-readiness audit (see prototype-to-production above);
  setup shown as a live board of plain-language cards, where mvpfy marks a task done only
  when it can verify the files it produced, and the final card — the app running with a
  working demo login — is the human's to close; one-click install of the required tools on
  macOS (git, Homebrew, GitHub CLI, Docker Desktop, Claude Code, Codex CLI) and in-app
  sign-in for GitHub, Claude and Codex.
- Maker: feature1 (https://feature1.ai). Source: https://github.com/feature1-ai/mvpfy.ai
- Download: https://github.com/feature1-ai/mvpfy.ai/releases/latest

## Guides

- [Prototype to production](https://mvpfy.ai/prototype-to-production.html): what breaks when
  an AI-built prototype (Lovable, Replit, Bolt, v0, Emergent) meets real users, why, and the
  steps to fix it.
